en: The Praise of Vajravilāsinī, composed by the feet of the great paṇḍita Vibhūticandra. Om. Homage to the glorious Vajrayoginī!

O You whose feet are worshipped by gods, asuras, and men; O You who have set Your feet to lifting up those submerged in worldly existence—to You I weep under the pretext of praise: do You not see that [suffering] is incessant and complete? 1.
O Mother Goddess, you scatter handfuls of grain; what dissatisfaction could there be for the son born of sacrifice?
O Vajravārāhī, you are the refuge of men, serpents, and gods who are devoted to your name. (2)
O Mother, O Goddess, fear of lions, elephants, fire, serpents, and thieves does not enter your heart at all;
look upon me—why do you endure my unbearable suffering? (3)
O you who hold the threatening vajra and skull-cup, who delight the wicked and ward off the Māras;
O you whose limbs possess hands and feet as fresh and tender as a young shoot, adorned with the three folds and the seven prominent curves.
With hands and feet purified of the state of grasped and grasper, webbed with a network of lines upon the fingers and toes;
with long sides of the hands and feet, and with disease, old age, night, and death destroyed. (5)
With dust raised upward and body hairs standing on end, you are the abode of nectar revealed through vajra-yoga;
you are red with the gaze of youthful rays of light, possessing the power to dispel the suffering of the worlds.
O lady with beautiful brows, slender waist, and delicate limbs; O bee-like one with eyes reaching to the tips of your ears!
Just as the world knows the *ḍākinī* to be the entirety of the universe without exception, so too it does not perceive your manifold disguises.

Without effort, there is the fulfillment of the world's welfare and the accomplishment of the desired objects of beings merely by thinking of them; yet the fool does not realize this, for just as in the rainy season no sprouts grow from stones, so too do his evil deeds bear no fruit.
For a sinful person who touches its power is like one blind to the sun and the moon; those ignorant of it do not recognize the wish-fulfilling gem, yet for the wise, its fruits indeed ripen.
To the one whose hands and feet are beautiful, marked with wheels, who has reduced all attachments to ashes with the fire of wisdom,
and who has [destroyed] the evil deeds committed through body, speech, and mind, as well as the entanglements of passion, hatred, and delusion— (10).

I declare this before you, O Goddess: as long as I do not fall into the side of miserable rebirths, my mind shall be fixed on the ultimate truth and my body shall be your altar; thus it shall never be exhausted by sin.

O you whose limbs are adorned with every primary mark, O vessel for all secondary characteristics, O you whose form is languid with the intoxication of fresh youth, O you whose cheeks are graced by a pair of swinging earrings! (12)
Upon her high hips and the weight of her firm breasts, where a necklace of pearls hung down from her neck like a goad;
upon her lotus-face kissed by the bee of Saṃvara, and upon her lotus-heart embraced by his two arms.

With eyes unblinking from the bliss of intense amorous passion, indifferent to loosened hair and discarded garments, she smiles as the mantra *hūṃ hūṃ* is uttered upon the moon-like face bitten by the serpent-like Heruka. (14)
Bearing the moon situated upon her husband’s crown, as if unable to endure it, does she perhaps eclipse both the sun and the moon with her body?
O Mother, whose form is incomparable in the world, contemplate that supreme reality which is your true nature. (15)

His speech is an ambrosia that extinguishes the fires of the afflictions and brings about the purification of those to be trained; he is like a lotus pond, possessing the stainless fragrance of a lotus, and is bound by compassion for the sake of the world. (16)
The drinking of the nectar residing within the divine vessel of ambrosia is the treasury of non-dual awakening for that world;
even the touch of every limb is signless, the mind being flooded by the ocean of the innate (*sahaja*). 17.
O Mother, what will you do with those three billion and six hundred million troops?
If you consider another [troop] to be more numerous than this, O Mother, then quickly give me that one instead.

The restraint of great bliss is the cessation of the network of channels; O Goddess, you are the hundredfold conceptualizations of existence, the emptiness-concentration that has cast off all duality. 19.
In the empty abyss, this vajra is described as liberated from duality;
divided by the vowels, it pervades all space, including existence and non-existence—that is the unfolding of reality. (20)

From that very source arise the liberations, all the factors conducive to enlightenment, and their antidotes, as well as the unique qualities of the Buddhas and the activity of maturing the multitudes of sentient beings. (21)

Or rather, whatever merit has been acquired by me through devotion to You— the departure via the three vehicles, and even the immeasurable [attainments] such as the "smoke" stage— may my mind become supremely devoted to You alone;
for You are the ocean of virtues, free from all defilement, and therefore You alone, and no other, are my kinsman.
The *Śrīvajravilāsinīstotra* from the *Guhyasamayasādhanatantra* is complete.
This is the work of the great paṇḍita Vibhūticandra.
